public_rationale: Anthropic had publicly launched and promoted customer offerings beyond Computer Use, including a Team plan, an iOS app, and Artifacts. That contradicts the categorical productization and exclusivity assertions under the ordinary reading of productize. Anthropic itself acknowledged that Computer Use was slow and error-prone, so this finding does not reject the narrower criticism of its performance. The specific timing comparison remains unverified.
limitations: The conclusion depends on productize meaning packaging and offering customer products, rather than establishing a profitable, differentiated business.
The OpenAI comparison is not separately resolved.
No outcome is proposed for the precise timing comparison.

statement.excerpt: Anthropic, much like OpenAI, has categorically failed to productize its Large Language Model, with the only product it appears to have pushed being Computer Use, a similarly-useless AI model that can sometimes successfully do in minutes what it takes you to do in seconds using a web browser.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading of productize is to package a model into usable products offered to customers. It does not necessarily mean achieving profitability.
Pushed means publicly launched and promoted. The qualification appears to have acknowledges uncertainty but still makes a checkable assertion.
The retrospective wording covers products launched before the post. The period ends on the preceding day to avoid uncertain ordering of same-day announcements.
The usefulness and timing assertions require separate evidence. A product announcement alone cannot establish either.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently complete product record shows no promoted customer product beyond Computer Use, while representative task evaluations establish the asserted lack of usefulness and minutes-versus-seconds performance.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Documented launches and promotion of customer products other than Computer Use contradict the categorical productization and exclusivity assertions. Matched task evaluations could separately contradict the performance assertion.

evidence.excerpt: a new Team plan and an iOS app.
evidence.explanation: Anthropic publicly promoted a team offering and mobile application. This contradicts the ordinary reading that Computer Use was its only promoted product.

The company explicitly invited customers to use another promoted application feature. This reinforces the contradiction of the exclusivity assertion, although a preview does not establish commercial success.
